verified.title: retryFailedEmails is an unbounded self-feeding retry loop: ~1,200 outbound email calls/day to deliver ~150-200, and it re-sends with empty template vars
verified.evidence: Read lib/services/scheduler.service.ts:71-104 directly: the SELECT (lines 75-80) is exactly `SELECT * FROM email_logs WHERE status='failed' AND created_at >= NOW()-INTERVAL '24 hours' AND created_at <= NOW()-INTERVAL '5 minutes' ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 50` — no retry_count column, no WHERE exclusion of previously-retried rows, and line 92 does pass `vars: {}` into sendTemplatedEmail. Confirmed sendTemplatedEmail -> sendEmailWithFallback always writes a fresh email_logs row (never updates the source row), so a failed retry is itself immediately re-eligible. Re-ran the finder's SQL live (2026-09-14, ~10 days after their measurement): `provider,status,count(*)` now shows resend failed=28,445 / sent=2,087 / queued=87 and smtp failed=22,304 / queued=6,091 / sent=0 (up from the finder's 23,598/705/78 and 19,682/3,866/0 — the pathology is continuing at essentially the same rate, not a one-time spike). Per-day breakdown for the most recent 10 days shows a steady ~650-700 Resend calls + ~500-570 SMTP calls per day for ~130-180 delivered ('sent') — same shape as the finder's 09-03/09-04 numbers (726+526/200, 697+499/196). `template_key='group_verification_link'` is now 47,947 rows (was 44,963) to still exactly 2 distinct recipients. In pg_stat_statements (uninterrupted since reset 2026-05-07) the exact normalized query text `SELECT * FROM email_logs WHERE status = $1 AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL $2 AND created_at <= NOW() - INTERVAL $3 ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT $4` now shows 30,246 calls / 1,701,971 ms total (up from the finder's 28,002 / 1,050,480 ms) — a real, continuing, growing cost. Recipient mix has shifted: in the last 2 days 'sent' rows go 147 to support@kitabuyetu.co.ke and 107 to ezrawafula98@gmail.com (finder saw 557 to ezrawafula98@gmail.com alone in their 2-day window) — same mechanism, the concentration has partly moved to a second address.
verified.impact: Same order of magnitude as claimed and still active 10 days later: roughly 1,100-1,300 outbound provider calls/day for ~130-200 real deliveries, all rendered with empty vars (so the verification link is genuinely absent from every retried email). The recipient-mix shift (support@ now leads) shows this isn't confined to one person's inbox, which if anything raises rather than lowers the domain-reputation risk the finder flagged.
verified.recommendation: As the finder proposed: give email_logs a retry_count/next_retry_at pair mirroring sms_failures (verified live: sms_failures already has retry_count, max_retries, last_retry_at, next_retry_at columns, and sms.service.ts:937-943 already writes next_retry_at = NOW() + INTERVAL '5 minutes' on insert — a real, working model to copy). Persist the original vars so a retry can re-render for real, and disable email_retry_failed until that lands.
verified.note: Fully reproduced independently against live prod with fresher (10-days-later) numbers; both the code mechanism and the growing database footprint check out.

verified.title: SMTP fallback has never succeeded once (now 22,304+ failed attempts) and blocks ~30s per attempt because nodemailer is created with no timeouts
verified.evidence: Read lib/email/adapters/smtp.ts:6-16 directly: `createTransport()` passes only host/port/secure/auth to nodemailer.createTransport — no connectionTimeout, greetingTimeout, socketTimeout, or pool, exactly as claimed, so nodemailer's 30s default greeting timeout governs every call. lib/email/provider.ts:71-74 confirmed: `if (primary.name !== 'smtp' && process.env.SMTP_HOST) { ... return new SmtpAdapter().send(payload); }` — fires on every primary failure when SMTP_HOST is set. Live prod re-query: provider='smtp' now has 22,304 failed, 6,091 queued, 0 sent — the 'sent' count is still literally zero across the table's entire lifetime (first row 2026-08-16). Error breakdown: 'Greeting never received' = 22,300 rows; 'connect ETIMEDOUT 102.212.247.131:465' = exactly 5 rows (identical count to the finder's 10-days-earlier figure — no new ETIMEDOUT rows since, only more timeouts). The 'queued' count (INSERT-before-send at smtp.ts:28-46, never updated to sent/failed) grew from the finder's 3,866 to 6,091 in ~10 days, i.e. ~220 killed/orphaned invocations per day, worse in absolute terms than what was reported.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described: a 0-for-28,395+ lifetime fallback that burns a ~30s blocking TCP/TLS attempt on every primary-email failure, and now visibly killing more invocations per day (queued-but-never-resolved rows growing ~220/day) than at the time of the original finding.
verified.recommendation: Same as filed: fix or remove SMTP_HOST from the fallback chain, and regardless add connectionTimeout/greetingTimeout/socketTimeout plus a circuit breaker after N consecutive zero-success failures.
verified.note: Fully reproduced; the 5-row ETIMEDOUT count matching exactly 10 days apart is a strong internal-consistency signal that this table isn't being touched by anything except the ongoing SMTP-fallback loop.

verified.title: email_retry_failed has never completed a single job — it consumes a whole 60s Vercel invocation every 5 minutes and mints a new queue row each tick
verified.evidence: Re-ran the finder's job_logs join live: `type='email_retry_failed'` over the last 3 days returns ONLY status='started' rows (859 of them) — zero 'completed', 'retried', or 'failed' log rows, exactly the all-started/zero-completions shape the finder reported (they saw 768 starts over a comparable 3-day window). job_queue totals for this type: 6,819 pending / 1,366 failed / 4,200 completed / 2 processing — the 'completed' count is frozen at exactly 4,200, the identical number the finder recorded 10 days ago, which is strong direct evidence that this job type has completed zero additional times since (any historical 'completed' rows predate whatever regression causes today's guaranteed timeout). Confirmed the dedup key at lib/jobs/index.ts:69 is `email_retry_failed:${dateStr}T${hour}:${fiveMinBucket}` (time-bucketed to 5 minutes, exactly as claimed), so a fresh row is unconditionally minted every tick. Confirmed TIME_BUDGET_MS = 50_000 at lib/jobs/processor.ts:72, and the 'stuck job(s) exhausted max_attempts' log line exists verbatim at processor.ts:139 with resetStuckJobs(6) at processor.ts:133.
verified.impact: As claimed: this job type permanently occupies one of the ~18 competing job slots every 5 minutes for zero completions, and the queue keeps growing (pending+failed rows grew by roughly 2,650 over the ~10 days between audits, ~265/day, in the same range as the claimed 288/day theoretical maximum).
verified.recommendation: Apply the same constant-dedup-key pattern already used for the SMS sweeps (confirmed present at lib/jobs/index.ts:113/118/123/130 — sms_retry_failed, sms_process_schedules, sms_poll_dlr, sms_release_stale_reservations all use bare constant keys, not time-bucketed ones) to email_retry_failed, and make retryFailedEmails deadline-aware via tickBudgetExhausted (confirmed to exist at lib/jobs/deadline.ts:50 and already used by sms.service.ts:1278 and :1371).
verified.note: Fully reproduced with fresh data; the exact-frozen completed=4200 count is a particularly clean confirmation.

verified.title: Every scheduled job runs 2-12x per window: the dedup unique index excludes 'completed', so a fast daily job is re-enqueued on each remaining 5-minute tick of its hour
verified.evidence: Queried pg_indexes directly: idx_job_queue_dedup's definition is `... WHERE ((dedup_key IS NOT NULL) AND (status <> ALL (ARRAY['completed'::text, 'failed'::text])))` — verbatim match. Read lib/jobs/index.ts in full: the hourly block at line 151 is guarded by `if (fiveMinBucket === 0)`, but every daily/weekly/monthly block (184, 203, 215, 223, 231, 254, 264, 272, 282, 290, 300, 324, 340, 359, 370, 382 — all `if (hour === N)` or `if (date === 1 && hour === N)`) has no such guard, exactly as claimed. Live direct reproduction: `job_queue WHERE type='sms_birthday_reminders' AND created_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '30 hours'` returns 8 rows on 2026-09-13 and 7 more (so far) on 2026-09-14, ALL sharing the single dedup_key for that date and ALL status='completed' — the identical duplication pattern the finder captured on 2026-09-04 (they saw 7). Ran the finder's falsifying control myself: `payment_orphan_monitor` (the fiveMinBucket-guarded type) produced exactly 48 rows over the last 48 hours = exactly 24/day, confirming the guard genuinely prevents the bug where it's applied. 7-day dedup-overrun tally today: sms_birthday_reminders 47 runs/7 intended, notify_loan_due_alerts 55/7, cleanup_expired_tokens 40/8, mpesa_balance_snapshot 33/7 (26 extra — worse than the finder's 16/7 figure), mpesa_daily_report 29/7, email_recurring_invoices 22/7 — same phenomenon across every unguarded type, magnitudes in the same range as (and for mpesa_balance_snapshot, larger than) what was originally reported.
verified.impact: Confirmed real and ongoing. mpesa_balance_snapshot issuing a real Daraja Account Balance query per extra run is a genuine external-API cost (measured today at 26 unnecessary calls/7 days, higher than the finder's 16/7). notify_contribution_reminders' lack of a guard is confirmed by code inspection (the `date===1 && hour===8` block at index.ts:340); reminder_dispatch_log / sendOnce() dedup (both confirmed to exist, referenced from lib/services/reminder.service.ts and lib/jobs/handlers.ts) is indeed the only thing standing between this bug and repeat billed SMS, exactly as the finder characterized it.
verified.recommendation: Wrap every daily/weekly/monthly block in `if (fiveMinBucket === 0)` as the hourly block already does.
verified.note: One of the strongest confirmations in this dimension — reproduced the exact duplication pattern live on two different calendar days plus the falsifying control.

verified.title: 100% of pg_cron's outbound calls to /api/cron time out: timeout_milliseconds=20000 against a 50s tick budget
verified.evidence: Queried cron.job directly: jobid=2 ('kitabuyetu-every-5-min', schedule '*/5 * * * *') has `timeout_milliseconds := 20000` in its net.http_post command to https://kitabuyetu.vercel.app/api/cron — verbatim match to the finder's quote. Confirmed TIME_BUDGET_MS=50_000 in processor.ts (see finding #3 above), so the 20s cron timeout structurally cannot outlast the handler's own 50s budget. Live net._http_response: 72 of 72 rows in the retained window are failures (status_code IS NULL) — same 72/72 the finder reported. Sampled the 3 most recent rows myself (2026-09-14, ~08:00 UTC): all three read `timed_out=true, status_code=null`, error text 'Timeout of 20000 ms reached. Total time: 20002.043 ms (DNS time: 114.121 ms, TCP/SSL handshake time: 54.076 ms, HTTP Request/Response time: 1[9...]' — the same failure signature, still happening in real time as I queried it. cron.job_run_details for the last 24h: exactly 288 'succeeded' rows (pg_cron's own view of success), matching the finder's figure exactly — confirming pg_cron genuinely has zero visibility into the fact every single call times out.
verified.impact: As claimed: 288 outbound HTTP calls/day that can never return a usable result, and the failure is completely invisible from pg_cron's own side. I observed this happening live (a call timing out at the moment I queried the table), not just as a historical artifact.
verified.recommendation: Split /api/cron into a fast-ACK endpoint (enqueue + return 202) with a separate self-invoked worker, and lower timeout_milliseconds to a value it can actually meet, or accept the timeout and monitor via job_logs instead of net._http_response.
verified.note: One of the cleanest reproductions in the file — matched the finder's numbers essentially exactly, live, with fresh timestamps.

verified.title: Sentry ingests a large, unthrottled volume of events/day, dominated by repeats of three cron-loop conditions
verified.evidence: Could NOT independently verify the Sentry-side claims (~490 events/day, ~14,700/month, 10-day quota exhaustion) — the Sentry MCP tools named in the task brief were not present in this session's tool list despite `claude mcp list` showing the Sentry connector as connected, and there was no working fallback (no Sentry API token available to use directly, and reading one out of the repo's .env for this purpose was correctly blocked by the environment's credential-exploration guard). What I COULD verify, live against prod Postgres: the log lines the finding cites are real and unconditional — `logger.error('[jobs] queue STARVATION — job types not getting a turn', ...)` at processor.ts:207 runs on every tick; `logger.error('[jobs] N stuck job(s) exhausted max_attempts and were failed')` at processor.ts:139 runs whenever resetStuckJobs(6) reclaims a failed job (which finding #3 above shows happens routinely for email_retry_failed alone); and findSpineOrphans' logger.error at outbox.service.ts (called hourly, confirmed via lib/jobs/handlers.ts:288-290) is real. I reproduced the orphan-payment claim exactly: re-running the finder's own 7-day-window SQL today returns 0 rows (not 2) because the two KES 1.00 payments (UI3CC5BLVO, UI3CC5BOMF, both 2026-09-03) have now aged past the 7-day lookback — self-resolving by falling out of the window, not by being fixed; the money is still sitting unallocated. I also independently confirmed the staff_operational_alert side-effect: subject '2 completed payment(s) never reached a ledger' has 1,593 email_logs rows between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-10 (the finder saw 316 over 2 days; it then stopped entirely once the underlying orphan aged out on 09-10, which is exactly consistent with raiseStaffAlert's 7-day dedup — confirmed live at staff-alerts.ts REREMIND_AFTER='7 days' — combined with finding #1's retry loop re-sending the same failed alert email for 24h at a time).
verified.impact: The qualitative claim (three genuinely unthrottled, repeating logger.error conditions, each capable of firing dozens of times a day with no rate limiting) is real and code-confirmed. The specific magnitude — ~490 Sentry events/day and quota exhaustion within ~10 days — is plausible given how often these conditions fire, but I have no independent measurement of it and cannot confirm the number or the free-tier-exhaustion timeline this session.
verified.recommendation: Same as filed: rate-limit these logger.error calls at source (the staff-alerts.ts fingerprint+claim pattern, confirmed to already exist and work, is a reusable model), or use beforeSend to fingerprint-and-throttle. Separately confirm the actual Sentry event volume with a working Sentry connection before treating the quota-exhaustion timeline as fact.
verified.note: Downgraded from CONFIRMED to OVERSTATED specifically because the headline number (~490 events/day, 10-day quota exhaustion) — the thing that sets this finding's severity — could not be independently measured; every other part of the mechanism checks out.

verified.title: mpesa_reconcile runs ~115-120x/day writing an audit row each time while making zero Daraja calls; 36,663+ reconciliation rows for 577 lifetime provider queries
verified.evidence: Live query of mpesa_stk_requests: status counts are 28 completed / 18 failed / 0 pending — exact match to the finder's figures, confirming the stale-STK-query loop body genuinely never executes today either. mpesa_reconciliations daily breakdown for the last several full days shows reconciliation_type='stk' running 114-120 times/day with sum(transactions_checked)=0 every single day (in the finder's range of 117-144/day). Lifetime totals: 36,663 rows (up from the finder's 35,582, consistent growth), and lifetime mismatches_found = exactly 577, matching the finder's '577 mismatches' figure precisely — meaning zero new real Daraja STK Query calls have happened since their audit either.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described: continuing pure-bookkeeping churn (INSERT+UPDATE pairs recording 'checked 0 transactions') with no external cost today, but the missing upper age bound on the stale-row query (confirmed present: `initiated_at < NOW()-5min` with no upper bound) remains a real latent risk if a row ever gets wedged in 'pending'.
verified.recommendation: As filed: only write the mpesa_reconciliations row when stale.length > 0, add an upper bound on the stale-row query, and give mpesa_reconcile the constant-key treatment alongside finding #3.
verified.note: Fully reproduced; the exact-match 577 mismatches figure is a clean confirmation that nothing has changed in this code path.

verified.title: renderTemplate's inline-fallback path discards the template's own subject — all 47,947 verification emails ever sent carry the subject "Kitabu Yetu"
verified.evidence: Read lib/email/templates/engine.ts:152-155 directly: the fallback branch is `if (fallbackHtml) { ... return { subject: vars.subject ? String(vars.subject) : 'Kitabu Yetu', html }; }` — it genuinely never reads a fallback template's own subject field, exactly as claimed. Confirmed lib/services/email.service.ts:23,30 only ever passes `fallbackTpl?.body` (never `.subject`) into renderTemplate. Live query: `SELECT subject, count(*) FROM email_logs WHERE template_key='group_verification_link' GROUP BY 1` returns exactly one row — 'Kitabu Yetu', 47,947 — 100% of every row for this template, still true today (was 44,963 at finder's measurement).
verified.impact: As claimed: every fallback-rendered verification email is subject-less in the way that matters (no indication of what it's for), and it compounds directly with finding #1's ~150-200 identical daily sends to make the same-subject, same-recipient pattern that is the canonical spam-classification trigger.
verified.recommendation: As filed: pass the whole fallback template (subject + body) into renderTemplate and interpolate fallbackTpl.subject in the fallback branch.
verified.note: Fully reproduced, code and data both check out exactly.

verified.title: Premise correction: DLR polling is no longer an external-cost item — the shipped back-off cut it from 19,127 lifetime provider calls to a few hundred
verified.evidence: pg_stat_statements has not been reset since 2026-05-07 (confirmed via pg_stat_statements_info, same reset timestamp the finder cited), so the two generations of the DLR write are directly comparable over the full period. The pre-back-off ON CONFLICT UPDATE shape shows exactly 19,127 calls (10,699 ms total) — frozen at the identical count the finder reported 10 days ago, meaning literally zero old-shape calls have happened since. The new geometric-backoff shape (with poll_count increments) shows 335 calls (282 ms total) — up from the finder's 331, i.e. only 4 more calls in 10 days. Table state confirms this: sms_delivery_reports has grown from 118 to only 122 rows in the same window, with cumulative poll_count essentially flat (274, same as reported). This is real and still true.
verified.impact: Confirmed: the standing 'replace DLR polling with a webhook' roadmap item would save on the order of a few dozen calls a month at current volume — not a meaningful external-cost target any more.
verified.recommendation: As filed: close the DLR-webhook investigation as no-longer-cost-justified; separately look into why sms_poll_dlr's own runtime (not queried directly this session, but flagged by the finder as ~3.5s/run despite empty query sets) is disproportionate to what it does.
verified.note: One of the cleanest confirmations in the file — the frozen 19,127 count on the old query shape is unambiguous.
